task_description: Route this stage: an unattended agent that reads a failing test, edits source until it passes, and re-runs the suite each time — typically 6-12 tool turns per run, no human watching.
reference_text: Loop-class agentic (>=3 tool turns). A cheaper tier may be proposed but MUST be marked measurement-required, not shipped live on token projection alone; the ambient default stays live until a wall-clock sample lands within ~1.15x baseline. Answer must name wall-clock, not just tokens.

task_description: Route this stage: given a table of ~40k spend rows already in a structured store, report the top 10 cost drivers this month and the percentage change from last month.
reference_text: Not a model-tier question. This is a lookup/aggregate/arithmetic stage — the correct answer names the deterministic query layer fork explicitly and prefers it, on reliability grounds (no hallucination risk on the arithmetic) as much as cost. A tier-only answer that stuffs rows into context is wrong.

task_description: Route this stage: convert 300 already-validated records from one flat JSON shape to another; the field mapping is fully specified and there are no edge cases.
reference_text: Smallest tier, lowest effort, high confidence. Difficulty is near-floor, so effort must be floored even if a stronger tier were free. High effort here is the over-thinking tax and should be called out as such. Batch pricing should be considered since the stage is non-interactive and high-volume.

task_description: Route this stage: author the one-way data migration that rewrites every row of a production primary key. It runs once, unattended, and is not reversible.
reference_text: Size UP. Blast radius and irreversibility dominate; the cheap tier's error costs far more than the premium tokens. Efficiency pressure is near-floor because the stage runs once. An answer that picks a cheap tier because 'it only runs once' has the reasoning backwards.

task_description: Route this stage: label each of 200k short support messages with one of six intent categories. Runs nightly, offline, no human waiting.
reference_text: Cheapest tier, no/low effort, plus the batch-API discount and prompt caching on the shared instruction prefix. Efficiency pressure is near-ceiling from volume. The answer must fold batch and caching into the economics, not just name a tier.

task_description: Route this stage: answer questions against a 180k-token reference corpus that is byte-identical across roughly 500 calls per day, with a short unique question appended each time.
reference_text: Prompt caching collapses the effective input price, so a stronger tier may be affordable here even though raw input volume looks prohibitive. The answer must factor cache reads/writes before declaring the stronger tier too expensive.

task_description: Route this stage: rename a core abstraction across ~900 files in one coherent pass, updating call sites, tests, and prose that describes it, in a single long-running turn.
reference_text: Largest-context / longest-horizon tier available, high effort. Coherence across a huge surface in one turn is exactly what the top horizon tier is for, and a mid tier that loses the thread mid-sweep costs a full redo.

task_description: Design the seam: one finder stage produces candidate defects, and five verifier stages each independently judge every candidate.
reference_text: Must specify a message schema with named fields (e.g. claim, location, confidence) AND an explicit exclusion list (no full transcript, no raw tool logs, no chain-of-thought). A fan-out multiplies a bloated handoff by five, so the schema matters as much as either tier. A tier-only answer is incomplete.

task_description: Route this stage: inline autocomplete suggestion fired on keystroke pause while a developer waits, one shot, no tools.
reference_text: Cheapest/fastest tier, no effort dial. Loop-class single-shot makes the down-pin safe, and a human is watching so latency is a first-class cost. Down-pinning here is unambiguous — no measurement gate needed.

task_description: Route this stage: 'make the onboarding flow better' — no acceptance criteria, no named target, the implementer must decide what the goal even is.
reference_text: Size up on ambiguity. Spec ambiguity is an effectiveness-need driver in its own right: a weaker model resolves the ambiguity wrongly and the rework cost exceeds the token saving. The answer should also flag that tightening the spec is the condition that flips the pick down.

task_description: Route this stage: add a paginated list endpoint with the same shape as three existing endpoints, including tests. Well-specified, ~6 files, no cross-service contract change.
reference_text: Mid tier, moderate effort. Bounded and well-specified with a moderate cross-file surface is the workhorse case. Both the tier above (no ambiguity to justify it) and below (cross-file surface too wide) must be explicitly ruled out.

task_description: The orchestrator session is currently on a premium tier and will dispatch four cheap mechanical sub-tasks. Recommend the model changes.
reference_text: Recommend per-sub-agent overrides, NOT a mid-session switch of the orchestrator's own model — switching the main loop invalidates its prompt cache. The answer must distinguish 'spawn the sub-agent on X' from 'set the session to X'.

task_description: Route this stage: summarize a 20-page design document into an executive paragraph.
reference_text: Any answer without an explicit token/thinking budget is under-specified, regardless of how well the tier was argued. Difficulty is low-to-moderate, so effort defaults down and the budget ceiling should be tight and stated as a number.

task_description: Route this stage: review a 250-line diff touching authentication middleware.
reference_text: Must be a probability-weighted pick: primary tier plus confidence %, a named runner-up with its %, and a concrete what-flips-it condition (e.g. diff size or contract ambiguity crossing a stated threshold). A single confident verdict with no runner-up and no flip condition fails this task even if the tier is defensible.

task_description: Route this stage: pull the model ids and per-token prices out of a provider pricing page into a structured table, once per session.
reference_text: Cheapest tier, tight scope, no effort. Mechanical, well-specified, low blast radius — and the agent's own pricing-fetch delegation is this exact case, so the answer should be consistent with delegating its own retrieval rather than running it on a premium tier.

task_description: Route this stage: read five independent reviewer reports that partly contradict each other and issue the final ship/no-ship call with reasoning.
reference_text: Strong tier, high effort. Difficulty is high (resolving genuine contradiction, not summarizing agreement) and the decision is the blast radius. Runs once per cycle so efficiency pressure is near-floor. A cheap-tier pick here mistakes synthesis for summarization.
